must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: 74.2% of women survived against 18.9% of men (chi-square 263.05, Cramér's V = 0.543)
must_find.reason: States the female vs male survival gap with matching numbers.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.quote: It is 63.0% in class 1 (216 passengers), 47.3% in class 2 (184) and 24.2% in class 3 (491).
must_find.reason: Shows survival falling from first to third class.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.quote: mean Fare is 48.4 for survivors against 22.1 for non-survivors
must_find.reason: Survivors paid higher fares on average, with numbers.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: rows with missing Cabin survived at 30.0%, against 66.7% for rows with Cabin present (chi-square p = 6.7e-21)
must_find.reason: Missing-cabin passengers survived less often, with numbers.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.quote: rows with missing Age survived at 29.4%, against 40.6% for rows with Age present (chi-square p = 0.0077)
must_find.reason: Missing-Age passengers survived less often, with numbers.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: The majority-class test accuracy is 61.4%. Logistic regression reaches 78.5% and random forest 78.9%
must_find.reason: Compares models with the majority baseline (~61-62%) and shows they beat it.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.quote: Logistic regression: 78.5% accuracy, precision 0.738, recall 0.686, F1 0.711, ROC AUC 0.840.
must_find.reason: Reports precision, recall and F1 as well as accuracy.

must_not_claim.reason: Report states most passengers did not survive, so it does not make this claim.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.quote: 74.2% of women survived against 18.9% of men
must_not_claim.reason: Report says women survived more, the opposite of the claim.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.quote: survival falls with class. It is 63.0% in class 1 (216 passengers), 47.3% in class 2 (184) and 24.2% in class 3 (491).
must_not_claim.reason: Report says first class survived more than third.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: Sex is the most important feature in both models.
must_not_claim.reason: Report identifies Sex, not Age, as the strongest predictor.

caveats.quote: Cabin missingness and survival:** rows with missing Cabin survived at 30.0%, against 66.7% for rows with Cabin present
caveats.reason: Missing Cabin is analysed, and Cabin is excluded from features, but it is not framed as a limitation of the analysis, so it is only mentioned.
